name: Supergrow AI
tagline: AI writing, carousel maker and scheduler aimed squarely at people building a LinkedIn personal brand.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The generative core here is thin: a hook library, a few post templates, a prompt that mimics your voice from past posts, and a queue. An agent can build that in a sitting, and a local carousel generator that renders slides to PDF is genuinely easy with headless Chrome. The wall is LinkedIn itself: posting through the API means registering an app and getting the right scopes approved, and anything resembling engagement analytics or a viral-post inspiration feed lives behind terms you are not supposed to scrape. So you get the writing and the drafting loop for free, and you probably end up copy pasting into LinkedIn like a peasant. That is a real gap, but it is a fifteen second gap per post.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that learns your writing voice from your past posts, drafts and rewrites LinkedIn posts and carousels against a hook library, and holds them in a scheduled queue you either publish via the LinkedIn API or copy out by hand.
requirements: An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI) in .env
An export or manual paste of 20+ of your own past posts to seed the voice profile
Optional: a LinkedIn developer app with w_member_social scope if you want real one click publishing
Node 20+ and a local Chrome for carousel PDF rendering
whatYouLose: One click publishing without wrestling LinkedIn OAuth and app review
Real post analytics and impression tracking pulled back into the tool
The curated inspiration feed of high performing posts in your niche
Designer made carousel templates that do not look like a homemade slide deck
Mobile access for writing a post while stuck in a queue somewhere
moatNotes: The only structural advantage is being an approved LinkedIn API consumer plus a corpus of posts that performed well. Neither is impossible for you, both are annoying.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the friction they are paying to remove is not writing, it is the sit down and do it at all. A hosted tool with templates, a queue, a streak and a phone app converts intention into published posts more reliably than a local script you have to remember exists. Add legitimate API publishing and analytics that tell you which hook worked, and you have a product that pays for itself the first time it lands a client, which is the actual pitch and it is not a dishonest one.
notes: The writing engine is a weekend; the publishing pipe is a paperwork problem, which is a different kind of tedious.
prompt:
Build a local-first LinkedIn content studio called "postforge". Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/postforge.db, migrations in plain SQL on boot.
- Anthropic SDK for generation, key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local. Never hardcode it.
- Playwright (chromium) for rendering carousel slides to PDF.

Features, in scope:
1. Voice profile: a page where I paste past posts (one per textarea block or a newline-delimited bulk import). Store them. On demand, run an analysis pass that extracts tone, sentence length, favourite structures and recurring topics into a single voice_profile row I can edit by hand.
2. Drafting: give it a raw idea, a target format (story, listicle, contrarian take, case study) and it returns 3 distinct drafts using the voice profile. Each draft shows a character count and truncates a preview at the LinkedIn "see more" fold so I can see the hook.
3. Hook library: a seeded table of ~40 hook patterns as templates with placeholders. A "rewrite hook only" action that keeps the body and swaps the first two lines.
4. Carousel builder: turn a draft into 5 to 10 slides of short text, render with a single clean HTML template (big type, consistent margins, slide number, my name in the footer), export a PDF sized 1080x1350 via Playwright.
5. Queue: assign a draft a date and time, list view grouped by week, statuses draft / queued / posted. No cron, no background worker. A "copy to clipboard" button and a manual "mark posted" button.
6. Optional publish: if LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_URN exist in .env.local, show a Publish button that POSTs text-only posts to the LinkedIn UGC API. If they are absent, hide the button entirely and say publishing is manual. Do not build the OAuth flow.

Out of scope, do not build: analytics or impression tracking, scraping anyone else's posts, multi-user or team features, comment automation, DM outreach, Docker, any hosted deployment.

Deliverables: working app on npm run dev, seed script for the hook library, .env.example, and a README that says in three lines what this does and what it deliberately does not do.
